Judith 15:10: you have done all this with your own hand; you have done great good to israel, and god is well pleased with it. may the almighty lord bless you forever!” and all the people said, “amen.”
Judith 15:11: all the people plundered the camp for thirty days. they gave judith the tent of holofernes and all his silver dinnerware, his beds, his bowls, and all his furniture. she took them and loaded her mules and hitched up her carts and piled the things on them.
Judith 15:12: all the women of israel gathered to see her and blessed her, and some of them performed a dance in her honor. she took ivy-wreathed wands in her hands and distributed them to the women who were with her,
Judith 15:13: and she and those who were with her crowned themselves with olive wreaths. she went before all the people in the dance, leading all the women, while all the men of israel followed, bearing their arms and wearing garlands and singing hymns.
Judith 15:14: judith offers her hymn of praise judith began this thanksgiving before all israel, and all the people loudly sang this song of praise.
Judith 16:1: and judith said, “begin a song to my god with tambourines; sing to my lord with cymbals. raise to him a new psalm; exalt him and call upon his name.
Judith 16:2: for the lord is a god who crushes wars; he sets up his camp among his people; he delivered me from the hands of my pursuers.
Judith 16:3: the assyrian came down from the mountains of the north; he came with myriads of his warriors; their numbers blocked up the wadis, and their cavalry covered the hills.
Judith 16:4: he boasted that he would burn up my territory and kill my young men with the sword and dash my infants to the ground and seize my children as plunder and take my virgins as spoil.
Judith 16:5: “but the lord almighty has foiled them by the hand of a woman.
Judith 16:6: for their mighty one did not fall by the hands of the young men, nor did the sons of the titans strike him down, nor did tall giants set upon him, but judith daughter of merari with the beauty of her countenance undid him.
Judith 16:7: “for she put away her widow’s clothing to exalt the oppressed in israel. she anointed her face with perfume;
Judith 16:8: she fastened her hair with a tiara and put on a linen gown to beguile him.
Judith 16:9: her sandal ravished his eyes, her beauty captivated his mind, and the sword severed his neck!
Judith 16:10: the persians trembled at her boldness; the medes were daunted at her daring.
Judith 16:11: “then my oppressed people shouted; my weak people cried out, and the enemy trembled; they lifted up their voices, and the enemy were turned back.
Judith 16:12: sons of female slaves pierced them through and wounded them like the children of fugitives; they perished before the army of my lord.
Judith 16:13: “i will sing to my god a new song: o lord, you are great and glorious, wonderful in strength, invincible.
Judith 16:14: let all your creatures serve you, for you spoke, and they were made. you sent forth your spirit, and it formed them; there is none that can resist your voice.
Judith 16:15: for the mountains shall be shaken to their foundations with the waters; before your glance the rocks shall melt like wax. but to those who fear you you show mercy.
Judith 16:16: for every sacrifice as a fragrant offering is a small thing, and the fat of all whole burnt offerings to you is a very little thing, but whoever fears the lord is great forever.
Judith 16:17: “woe to the nations that rise up against my people! the lord almighty will take vengeance on them in the day of judgment; he will send fire and worms into their flesh; they shall weep in pain forever.”
Judith 16:18: when they arrived at jerusalem, they worshiped god. as soon as the people were purified, they offered their burnt offerings, their freewill offerings, and their gifts.
Judith 16:19: judith also dedicated to god all the possessions of holofernes that the people had given her, and the canopy that she had taken for herself from his bedchamber she gave as a votive offering.
Judith 16:20: for three months the people continued feasting in jerusalem before the sanctuary, and judith remained with them.
Judith 16:21: the renown and death of judith after this they all returned home to their own inheritances. judith went to bethulia and remained on her estate. for the rest of her life she was honored throughout the whole country.
Judith 16:22: many desired to marry her, but she gave herself to no man all the days of her life after her husband manasseh died and was gathered to his people.
Judith 16:23: she became more and more famous and grew old in her husband’s house, reaching the age of one hundred five. she set her maid free. she died in bethulia, and they buried her in the cave of her husband manasseh,
Judith 16:24: and the house of israel mourned her for seven days. before she died she distributed her property to all those who were next of kin to her husband manasseh and to her own nearest kindred.
Judith 16:25: no one ever again spread terror among the israelites during the lifetime of judith or for a long time after her death.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:1: a copy of a letter that jeremiah sent to those who were to be taken to babylon as exiles by the king of the babylonians, to give them the message that god had commanded him. the people face a long captivity because of the sins that you have committed before god, you will be taken to babylon as exiles by nebuchadnezzar, king of the babylonians.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:2: therefore when you have come to babylon you will remain there for many years, for a long time, up to seven generations; after that i will bring you away from there in peace.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:3: now in babylon you will see gods made of silver and gold and wood that people carry on their shoulders and that cause the nations to fear.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:4: so beware of becoming at all like the foreigners or of letting fear of these gods possess you
Letter of Jeremiah 1:5: when you see the multitude before and behind them worshiping them. but say in your heart, “it is you, o lord, whom we must worship.”
Letter of Jeremiah 1:6: for my angel is with you, and he is watching over your lives.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:7: the helplessness of idols their tongues are smoothed by the carpenter, and they themselves are overlaid with gold and silver, but they are false and cannot speak.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:8: people take gold and make crowns for the heads of their gods, as they might for a young woman who loves ornaments.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:9: sometimes the priests secretly take gold and silver from their gods and spend it on themselves
Letter of Jeremiah 1:10: or even give some of it to the prostitutes on the terrace. they deck their gods out with garments like humans—these gods of silver and gold and wood
Letter of Jeremiah 1:11: that cannot save themselves from rust and decay. when they have been dressed in purple robes,
Letter of Jeremiah 1:12: their faces are wiped because of the dust from the temple, which is thick upon them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:13: one of them holds a scepter like a district judge but is unable to destroy anyone who offends it.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:14: another has a dagger in its right hand and an ax but cannot defend itself from war and robbers.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:15: from this it is evident that they are not gods, so do not fear them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:16: for just as someone’s dish is useless when it is broken,
Letter of Jeremiah 1:17: so are their gods when they have been set up in the temples. their eyes are full of the dust raised by the feet of those who enter. and just as the gates are shut on every side against anyone who has offended a king, as though under sentence of death, so the priests make their temples secure with doors and locks and bars in order that they may not be plundered by robbers.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:18: they light more lamps for them than they light for themselves, though their gods can see none of them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:19: they are just like a beam of the temple, but their hearts, it is said, are eaten away when crawling creatures from the earth devour them and their robes. they do not notice
Letter of Jeremiah 1:20: when their faces have been blackened by the smoke of the temple.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:21: bats, swallows, and birds alight on their bodies and heads, and so do cats.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:22: from this you will know that they are not gods, so do not fear them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:23: as for the gold that they wear for beauty, it will not shine unless someone wipes off the tarnish, for even when they were being cast, they did not feel it.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:24: they are bought without regard to cost, but there is no breath in them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:25: having no feet, they are carried on the shoulders of others, revealing to humans their worthlessness. and those who serve them are put to shame
Letter of Jeremiah 1:26: because, if any of these gods falls to the ground, they themselves must pick it up. if anyone sets it upright, it cannot move itself, and if it is tipped over, it cannot straighten itself. gifts are placed before them just as before the dead.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:27: the priests sell the sacrifices that are offered to these gods and use the money themselves. likewise their wives preserve some of the meat with salt but give none to the poor or helpless.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:28: sacrifices to them may even be touched by women during their periods or after giving birth. since you know by these things that they are not gods, do not fear them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:29: for how can they be called gods? women serve meals for gods of silver and gold and wood,
Letter of Jeremiah 1:30: and in their temples the priests sit with their clothes torn, their heads and beards shaved, and their heads uncovered.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:31: they howl and shout before their gods as some do at a funeral banquet.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:32: the priests take some of the clothing of their gods to clothe their wives and children.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:33: whether one does evil to them or good, they will not be able to repay it. they cannot set up a king or depose one.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:34: likewise, they are not able to give either wealth or money; if one makes a vow to them and does not keep it, they will not require it.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:35: they cannot save anyone from death or rescue the weak from the strong.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:36: they cannot restore sight to the blind; they cannot rescue one who is in distress.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:37: they cannot take pity on a widow or do good to an orphan.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:38: these things that are made of wood and overlaid with gold and silver are like stones from the mountain, and those who serve them will be put to shame.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:39: why then must anyone think that they are gods or call them gods? the foolishness of worshiping idols besides, even the chaldeans themselves dishonor them, for when they see someone who cannot speak, they bring bel and pray that the mute may speak, as though bel were able to understand!
Letter of Jeremiah 1:40: yet they themselves cannot perceive this and abandon them, for they have no sense.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:41: and the women, with cords around them, sit along the passageways, burning bran for incense.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:42: when one of them is led off by one of the passers-by and is taken to bed by him, she derides the woman next to her because she was not as attractive as herself and her cord was not broken.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:43: whatever is done for these idols is false. why then must anyone think that they are gods or call them gods?
Letter of Jeremiah 1:44: they are made by carpenters and goldsmiths; they can be nothing but what the artisans wish them to be.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:45: those who make them will certainly not live very long themselves;
Letter of Jeremiah 1:46: how then can the things that are made by them be gods? they have left only lies and reproach for those who come after.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:47: for when war or calamity comes upon them, the priests consult together as to where they can hide themselves and their gods.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:48: how then can one fail to see that these are not gods, for they cannot save themselves from war or calamity?
Letter of Jeremiah 1:49: since they are made of wood and overlaid with gold and silver, it will afterward be known that they are false.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:50: it will be manifest to all the nations and kings that they are not gods but the work of human hands and that there is no work of god in them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:51: who, then, does not know that they are not gods?
Letter of Jeremiah 1:52: for they cannot set up a king over a country or give rain to people.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:53: they cannot judge their own cause or deliver one who is wronged, for they have no power;
Letter of Jeremiah 1:54: they are like crows between heaven and earth. when fire breaks out in a temple of wooden gods overlaid with gold or silver, their priests will flee and escape, but the gods will be burned up like timbers.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:55: besides, they can offer no resistance to king or enemy. why then must anyone admit or think that they are gods?
Letter of Jeremiah 1:56: gods made of wood and overlaid with silver and gold are unable to save themselves from thieves or robbers.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:57: anyone who can will strip them of their gold and silver and of the robes they wear and go off with this plunder, and they will not be able to help themselves.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:58: so it is better to be a king who shows his courage or a household utensil that serves its owner’s need than to be these false gods, better even the door of a house that protects its contents than these false gods, better also a wooden pillar in a palace than these false gods.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:59: for sun and moon and stars are bright and, when sent to do a service, they are obedient.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:60: so also the lightning when it flashes is widely seen, and the wind likewise blows in every land.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:61: when god commands the clouds to go over the whole world, they carry out his command.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:62: and the fire sent from above to consume mountains and woods does what it is ordered. but these idols are not to be compared with them in appearance or power.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:63: therefore one must not think that they are gods nor call them gods, for they are unable either to decide a case or to do good to anyone.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:64: since you know, then, that they are not gods, do not fear them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:65: they can neither curse nor bless kings;
Letter of Jeremiah 1:66: they cannot show signs in the heavens for the nations or shine like the sun or give light like the moon.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:67: the wild animals are better than they are, for they can flee to shelter and help themselves.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:68: so we have no evidence whatever that they are gods; therefore do not fear them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:69: like a scarecrow in a cucumber bed that guards nothing, so are their gods of wood, overlaid with gold and silver.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:70: in the same way, their gods of wood, overlaid with gold and silver, are like a thornbush in a garden on which every bird perches or like a corpse thrown out in the darkness.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:71: from the purple and linen that rot upon them you will know that they are not gods, and they will finally be consumed themselves and be a reproach in the land.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:72: better, therefore, is someone upright who has no idols; such a person will be far above reproach.
Prayer of Azariah 1:1: (additions to daniel, inserted between and ) the prayer of azariah in the furnace they walked around in the midst of the flames, singing hymns to god and blessing the lord.
Prayer of Azariah 1:2: then azariah stood still in the fire and prayed aloud:
Prayer of Azariah 1:3: “blessed are you, o lord, god of our ancestors, and worthy of praise, and glorious is your name forever!
Prayer of Azariah 1:4: for you are just in all you have done; all your works are true and your ways right, and all your judgments are true.
Prayer of Azariah 1:5: you have executed true judgments in all you have brought upon us and upon jerusalem, the holy city of our ancestors; by a true judgment you have brought all this upon us because of our sins.
Prayer of Azariah 1:6: for we have sinned and broken your law in turning away from you; in all matters we have sinned grievously.
Prayer of Azariah 1:7: we have not obeyed your commandments; we have not kept them or done what you have commanded us for our own good.
Prayer of Azariah 1:8: so all that you have brought upon us and all that you have done to us, you have done by a true judgment.
Prayer of Azariah 1:9: you have handed us over to our enemies, lawless and hateful rebels, and to an unjust king, the most wicked in all the world.
Prayer of Azariah 1:10: and now we cannot open our mouths; we, your servants who worship you, bear shame and reproach.
Prayer of Azariah 1:11: for your name’s sake do not give us up forever, and do not annul your covenant.
Prayer of Azariah 1:12: do not withdraw your mercy from us, for the sake of abraham your beloved and for the sake of isaac your servant and israel your holy one,
Prayer of Azariah 1:13: to whom you promised to multiply their descendants like the stars of heaven and like the sand on the shore of the sea.
Prayer of Azariah 1:14: for we, o lord, have become fewer than any other nation and are brought low this day in all the world because of our sins.
Prayer of Azariah 1:15: in our day we have no ruler, or prophet, or leader, no burnt offering, or sacrifice, or oblation, or incense, no place to make an offering before you and to find mercy.
Prayer of Azariah 1:16: yet with a contrite heart and a humble spirit may we be accepted,
Prayer of Azariah 1:17: as though it were with burnt offerings of rams and bulls or with tens of thousands of fat lambs; such may our sacrifice be in your sight today, and may we unreservedly follow you, for no shame will come to those who trust in you.
Prayer of Azariah 1:18: and now with all our heart we follow you; we fear you and seek your presence.
Prayer of Azariah 1:19: do not put us to shame, but deal with us in your patience and in your abundant mercy.
Prayer of Azariah 1:20: deliver us in accordance with your marvelous works, and bring glory to your name, o lord.
Prayer of Azariah 1:21: let all who do harm to your servants be put to shame; let them be disgraced and deprived of all power, and let their strength be broken.
Prayer of Azariah 1:22: let them know that you alone are the lord god, glorious over the whole world.”
Prayer of Azariah 1:23: the song of the three jews now the king’s servants who threw them in kept stoking the furnace with naphtha, pitch, tinder, and brushwood.
Prayer of Azariah 1:24: and the flames poured out above the furnace forty-nine cubits
Prayer of Azariah 1:25: and spread out and burned those chaldeans who were caught near the furnace.
Prayer of Azariah 1:26: but the angel of the lord came down into the furnace to be with azariah and his companions and drove the fiery flame out of the furnace
Prayer of Azariah 1:27: and made the inside of the furnace as though a moist wind were whistling through it. the fire did not touch them at all and caused them no pain or distress.
Prayer of Azariah 1:28: then the three with one voice praised and glorified and blessed god in the furnace:
Prayer of Azariah 1:29: “blessed are you, o lord, god of our ancestors, and to be praised and highly exalted forever; and blessed is your glorious, holy name, and to be highly praised and highly exalted forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:30: blessed are you in the temple of your holy glory, and to be extolled and highly glorified forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:31: blessed are you who look into the depths from your throne on the cherubim, and to be praised and highly exalted forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:32: blessed are you on the throne of your kingdom, and to be extolled and highly exalted forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:33: blessed are you in the firmament of heaven, and to be sung and glorified forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:34: “bless the lord, all you works of the lord; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:35: bless the lord, you heavens; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:36: bless the lord, you angels of the lord; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:37: bless the lord, all you waters above the heavens; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:38: bless the lord, all you powers of the lord; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:39: bless the lord, sun and moon; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:40: bless the lord, stars of heaven; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:41: “bless the lord, all rain and dew; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:42: bless the lord, all you winds; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:43: bless the lord, fire and heat; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:44: bless the lord, winter cold and summer heat; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:45: bless the lord, dews and falling snow; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:46: bless the lord, nights and days; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:47: bless the lord, light and darkness; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:48: bless the lord, ice and cold; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:49: bless the lord, frosts and snows; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:50: bless the lord, lightnings and clouds; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:51: “let the earth bless the lord; let it sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:52: bless the lord, mountains and hills; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:53: bless the lord, all that grows in the ground; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:54: bless the lord, seas and rivers; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:55: bless the lord, you springs; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:56: bless the lord, you sea monsters and all that swim in the waters; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:57: bless the lord, all birds of the air; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:58: bless the lord, all wild animals and cattle; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:59: “bless the lord, all people on earth; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:60: bless the lord, o israel; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:61: bless the lord, you priests of the lord; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:62: bless the lord, you servants of the lord; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:63: bless the lord, spirits and souls of the righteous; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:64: bless the lord, you who are holy and humble in heart; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:65: “bless the lord, hananiah, azariah, and mishael; sing praise to him and highly exalt him forever. for he has rescued us from hades and saved us from the power of death and delivered us from the midst of the burning fiery furnace; from the midst of the fire he has delivered us.
Prayer of Azariah 1:66: give thanks to the lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
Prayer of Azariah 1:67: all who worship the lord, bless the god of gods, sing praise to him and give thanks to him, for his mercy endures forever.”
Prayer of Manasseh 1:1: ascription of praise o lord almighty, god of our ancestors, of abraham and isaac and jacob and of their righteous offspring,
Prayer of Manasseh 1:2: you who made heaven and earth with all their order,
Prayer of Manasseh 1:3: who shackled the sea by your word of command, who confined the deep and sealed it with your terrible and glorious name,
Prayer of Manasseh 1:4: at whom all things shudder and tremble before your power,
Prayer of Manasseh 1:5: for your glorious splendor cannot be borne, and the wrath of your threat to sinners is unendurable;
Prayer of Manasseh 1:6: yet immeasurable and unsearchable is your promised mercy,
Prayer of Manasseh 1:7: for you are the lord most high, of great compassion, long-suffering, and very merciful, and you relent at human suffering. o lord, according to your great goodness you have promised repentance and forgiveness to those who have sinned against you, and in the multitude of your mercies you have appointed repentance for sinners, so that they may be saved.
Prayer of Manasseh 1:8: therefore you, o lord, god of the righteous, have not appointed repentance for the righteous, for abraham and isaac and jacob, who did not sin against you, but you have appointed repentance for me, who am a sinner.
Prayer of Manasseh 1:9: confession of sins for the sins i have committed are more in number than the sand of the sea; my transgressions are multiplied, o lord, they are multiplied! i am not worthy to look up and see the height of heaven because of the multitude of my iniquities.
Prayer of Manasseh 1:10: i am weighted down with many an iron fetter, so that i am rejected because of my sins, and i have no relief, for i have provoked your wrath and have done what is evil in your sight, setting up abominations and multiplying offenses.
Prayer of Manasseh 1:11: supplication for pardon and now i bend the knee of my heart, imploring you for your kindness.
Prayer of Manasseh 1:12: i have sinned, o lord, i have sinned, and i acknowledge my transgressions.
Prayer of Manasseh 1:13: i earnestly implore you, forgive me, o lord, forgive me! do not destroy me with my transgressions! do not be angry with me forever or store up evil for me; do not condemn me to the depths of the earth. for you, o lord, are the god of those who repent,
Prayer of Manasseh 1:14: and in me you will manifest your goodness, for, unworthy as i am, you will save me according to your great mercy,
Prayer of Manasseh 1:15: and i will praise you continually all the days of my life. for all the host of heaven sings your praise, and yours is the glory forever. amen.
Psalm 151 1:1: this psalm is ascribed to david as his own composition (though it is outside the number ), after he had fought in single combat with goliath. 151 i was small among my brothers and the youngest in my father’s house; i tended my father’s sheep.
Psalm 151 1:2: my hands made a harp; my fingers fashioned a lyre.
Psalm 151 1:3: and who will tell my lord? the lord himself; it is he who hears.
Psalm 151 1:4: it was he who sent his messenger and took me from my father’s sheep and anointed me with his anointing oil.
Psalm 151 1:5: my brothers were handsome and tall, but the lord was not pleased with them.
Psalm 151 1:6: i went out to meet the foreigner, and he cursed me by his idols.
Psalm 151 1:7: but i drew his own sword; i beheaded him and removed disgrace from the people of israel.
Sirach 1:1: all wisdom is from the lord, and with him it remains forever.
Sirach 1:2: the sand of the sea, the drops of rain, and the days of eternity—who can count them?
Sirach 1:3: the height of heaven, the breadth of the earth, the abyss, and wisdom —who can search them out?
Sirach 1:4: wisdom was created before all things and prudent understanding from eternity.
Sirach 1:6: the root of wisdom—to whom has it been revealed? her subtleties—who knows them?
Sirach 1:8: there is but one who is wise, greatly to be feared, seated upon his throne: the lord.
Sirach 1:9: it is he who created her; he saw her and took her measure; he poured her out upon all his works,
Sirach 1:10: upon all the living according to his gift; he lavished her upon those who love him.
Sirach 1:11: fear of the lord is true wisdom the fear of the lord is glory and exultation and gladness and a crown of rejoicing.
Sirach 1:12: the fear of the lord delights the heart and gives gladness and joy and long life.
Sirach 1:13: those who fear the lord will have a happy end; on the day of their death they will be blessed.
Sirach 1:14: to fear the lord is the beginning of wisdom; she is created with the faithful in the womb.
Sirach 1:15: she made among humans an eternal foundation, and among their descendants she will abide faithfully.
Sirach 1:16: to fear the lord is fullness of wisdom; she inebriates mortals with her fruits;
Sirach 1:17: she fills their whole house with desirable goods and their storehouses with her produce.
Sirach 1:18: the fear of the lord is the crown of wisdom, making peace and perfect health to flourish.
Sirach 1:19: she rained down knowledge and discerning comprehension, and she heightened the glory of those who held her fast.
Sirach 1:20: to fear the lord is the root of wisdom, and her branches are long life.
Sirach 1:22: unjust anger cannot be justified, for anger tips the scale to one’s ruin.
Sirach 1:23: those who are patient stay calm until the right moment, and then cheerfulness comes back to them.
Sirach 1:24: they hold back their words until the right moment, and then the lips of many tell of their good sense.
Sirach 1:25: in the treasuries of wisdom is insightful analogy, but godliness is an abomination to a sinner.
Sirach 1:26: if you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and the lord will lavish her upon you.
Sirach 1:27: for the fear of the lord is wisdom and discipline; fidelity and humility are his delight.
Sirach 1:28: do not disobey the fear of the lord; do not approach him with a divided mind.
Sirach 1:29: do not be a hypocrite before others, and keep watch over your lips.
Sirach 1:30: do not exalt yourself, or you may fall and bring dishonor upon yourself. the lord will reveal your secrets and overthrow you before the whole congregation, because you did not come in the fear of the lord, and your heart was full of deceit.
Sirach 2:1: my child, when you come to serve the lord, prepare yourself for testing.
Sirach 2:2: set your heart right and be steadfast, and do not be impetuous in time of calamity.
Sirach 2:3: cling to him and do not depart, so that your last days may be prosperous.
Sirach 2:4: accept whatever befalls you, and in times of humiliation be patient.
Sirach 2:5: for gold is tested in the fire, and those found acceptable, in the furnace of humiliation.
Sirach 2:6: trust in him, and he will help you; make your ways straight and hope in him.
Sirach 2:7: you who fear the lord, wait for his mercy; do not stray, or else you may fall.
Sirach 2:8: you who fear the lord, trust in him, and your reward will not be lost.
Sirach 2:9: you who fear the lord, hope for good things, for lasting joy and mercy.
Sirach 2:10: consider the generations of old and see: has anyone trusted in the lord and been disappointed? or has anyone persevered in the fear of the lord and been forsaken? or has anyone called upon him and been neglected?
Sirach 2:11: for the lord is compassionate and merciful; he forgives sins and saves in time of distress.
Sirach 2:12: woe to timid hearts and to slack hands and to the sinner who walks a double path!
Sirach 2:13: woe to the fainthearted who have no trust! therefore they will have no shelter.
Sirach 2:14: woe to you who have lost patience! what will you do when the lord’s reckoning comes?
Sirach 2:15: those who fear the lord will not disobey his words, and those who love him will keep his ways.
Sirach 2:16: those who fear the lord will seek his favor, and those who love him will be filled with his law.
Sirach 2:17: those who fear the lord will prepare their hearts and will humble themselves before him.
Sirach 2:18: let us fall into the hands of the lord but not into the hands of mortals, for equal to his majesty is his mercy.
Sirach 3:1: listen to me your father, o children; act accordingly, that you may be safe.
Sirach 3:2: for the lord honors a father above his children, and he confirms a mother’s judgment over her sons.
Sirach 3:3: those who honor their father atone for sins,
Sirach 3:4: and those who respect their mother are like those who lay up treasure.
Sirach 3:5: those who honor their father will have joy in their children, and when they pray they will be heard.
Sirach 3:6: those who respect their father will have long life, and those who honor their mother obey the lord;
Sirach 3:7: they will serve their parents as their masters.
Sirach 3:8: honor your father by word and deed, that his blessing may come upon you.
Sirach 3:9: for a father’s blessing strengthens the houses of the children, but a mother’s curse uproots their foundations.
Sirach 3:10: do not glorify yourself by your father’s dishonor, for your father’s dishonor is no glory to you.
Sirach 3:11: the honor of one’s father is one’s own glory, and a mother dishonored is a disgrace to her children.
Sirach 3:12: my child, help your father in his old age, and do not grieve him as long as he lives;
Sirach 3:13: even if his mind fails, be patient with him; do not despise him because you have all your faculties.
Sirach 3:14: for kindness to a father will not be forgotten and will be credited to you against your sins;
Sirach 3:15: in the day of your distress it will be remembered in your favor; like frost in fair weather, your sins will melt away.
Sirach 3:16: whoever forsakes a father is like a blasphemer, and whoever angers a mother is cursed by the lord.
Sirach 3:17: humility my child, perform your tasks with humility; then you will be loved more than a giver of gifts.
Sirach 3:18: the greater you are, the more you must humble yourself; so you will find favor in the sight of the lord.
Sirach 3:20: for great is the might of the lord, but by the humble he is glorified.
Sirach 3:21: neither seek what is too difficult for you nor investigate what is beyond your power.
Sirach 3:22: reflect upon what you have been commanded, for what is hidden is not your concern.
Sirach 3:23: in matters greater than your own affairs, do not meddle, for things beyond human understanding have been shown you.
Sirach 3:24: for their conceit has led many astray, and wrong opinion has impaired their judgment.
Sirach 3:25: without eyes there is no light; without knowledge there is no wisdom.
Sirach 3:26: a stubborn mind will fare badly at the end, and whoever loves danger will perish in it.
Sirach 3:27: a stubborn mind will be burdened by troubles, and the sinner adds sin to sins.
Sirach 3:28: when calamity befalls the proud, there is no healing, for an evil plant has taken root in him.
Sirach 3:29: the mind of the intelligent appreciates proverbs, and an attentive ear is the desire of the wise.
Sirach 3:30: alms for the poor as water extinguishes a blazing fire, so almsgiving atones for sin.
Sirach 3:31: those who repay favors give thought to the future; when they fall they will find support.
Sirach 4:1: my child, do not cheat the poor of their living, and do not keep needy eyes waiting.
Sirach 4:2: do not grieve the hungry or anger one in need.
Sirach 4:3: do not add to the troubles of the angry or delay giving to the needy.
Sirach 4:4: do not reject a suppliant in distress or turn your face away from the poor.
Sirach 4:5: do not avert your eye from the needy, and give no one reason to curse you,
Sirach 4:6: for if in bitterness of soul some should curse you, their creator will hear their prayer.
Sirach 4:7: endear yourself to the congregation; bow your head low to the great.
Sirach 4:8: give a hearing to the poor, and return their greeting kindly.
Sirach 4:9: rescue the oppressed from the oppressor, and do not be hesitant in giving a verdict.
Sirach 4:10: be a father to orphans, and be like a husband to their mother; you will then be like a son of the most high, and he will love you more than does your mother.
Sirach 4:11: the rewards of wisdom wisdom teaches her children and takes hold of those who seek her.
Sirach 4:12: whoever loves her loves life, and those who seek her from early morning will be filled with joy.
Sirach 4:13: whoever holds her fast inherits glory, and the lord blesses the place she enters.
Sirach 4:14: those who serve her minister to the holy one; the lord loves those who love her.
Sirach 4:15: whoever obeys her will judge the nations, and whoever listens to her will live securely.
Sirach 4:16: if they remain faithful, they will inherit her; their descendants will also obtain her.
Sirach 4:17: for at first she will walk with them in disguise; she will bring fear and dread upon them and will torment them by her discipline until she trusts them, and she will test them with her ordinances.
Sirach 4:18: then she will come straight back to them again and gladden them and will reveal her secrets to them.
Sirach 4:19: if they go astray, she will forsake them and hand them over to their ruin.
Sirach 4:20: watch for the opportune time, and beware of evil, and do not be ashamed to be yourself.
Sirach 4:21: for there is a shame that leads to sin, and there is a shame that is glory and favor.
Sirach 4:22: do not show partiality to your own harm or deference to your downfall.
Sirach 4:23: do not refrain from speaking at the proper moment, and do not hide your wisdom.
Sirach 4:24: for wisdom becomes known through speech and education through the words of the tongue.
Sirach 4:25: never speak against the truth, but be ashamed of your ignorance.
Sirach 4:26: do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not try to stop the current of a river.
Sirach 4:27: do not subject yourself to a fool or show partiality to a ruler.
Sirach 4:28: fight to the death for truth, and the lord god will fight for you.
Sirach 4:29: do not be reckless in your speech or sluggish and remiss in your deeds.
Sirach 4:30: do not be like a lion in your home or suspicious of your slaves.
Sirach 4:31: do not let your hand be stretched out to receive and closed when it is time to give back.
Sirach 5:1: do not rely on your wealth or say, “i have enough.”
Sirach 5:2: do not follow your inclination and strength in pursuing the desires of your heart.
Sirach 5:3: do not say, “who can have power over me?” for the lord will surely punish you.
Sirach 5:4: do not say, “i sinned, yet what has happened to me?” for the lord is slow to anger.
Sirach 5:5: do not be so confident of forgiveness that you add sin to sins.
Sirach 5:6: do not say, “his mercy is great; he will forgive the multitude of my sins,” for both mercy and wrath are with him, and his anger will rest on sinners.
Sirach 5:7: do not delay to turn back to the lord, and do not postpone it from day to day, for suddenly the wrath of the lord will come forth, and at the time of punishment you will perish.
Sirach 5:8: do not rely on dishonest wealth, for it will not benefit you on the day of calamity.
Sirach 5:9: do not winnow in every wind or follow every path.
Sirach 5:10: stand firm in what you know, and let your speech be consistent.
Sirach 5:11: be quick to hear, and utter a reply patiently.
Sirach 5:12: if you understand, answer your neighbor, but if not, put your hand over your mouth.
Sirach 5:13: honor and dishonor come from speaking, and the tongue of mortals may be their downfall.
Sirach 5:14: do not be called double-tongued and do not lay traps with your tongue, for shame comes to the thief and severe condemnation to the double-tongued.
Sirach 5:15: in great and small matters cause no harm,
Sirach 6:1: and do not become an enemy instead of a friend, for a bad name incurs shame and reproach; so it is with the double-tongued sinner.
Sirach 6:2: do not fall into the grip of passion, or you may be torn apart as by a bull.
Sirach 6:3: your leaves will be devoured and your fruit destroyed, and you will be left like a withered tree.
Sirach 6:4: strong passion destroys those who have it and makes them the laughingstock of their enemies.
Sirach 6:5: friendship, false and true pleasant speech multiplies friends, and a gracious tongue multiplies courtesies.
Sirach 6:6: let those who are at peace with you be many, but let your advisers be one in a thousand.
Sirach 6:7: when you gain friends, gain them through testing, and do not trust them hastily.
Sirach 6:8: for there are friends who are such when it suits them, but they will not stand by you in time of trouble.
Sirach 6:9: and there are friends who turn to enmity and tell of the quarrel to your disgrace.
Sirach 6:10: and there are friends who are companions at the table, but they will not stand by you in time of trouble.
Sirach 6:11: when you are prosperous, they become your second self and boldly command your slaves,
Sirach 6:12: but if you are brought low, they turn against you and hide themselves from you.
Sirach 6:13: keep away from your enemies, and be on guard with your friends.
Sirach 6:14: faithful friends are a sturdy shelter; whoever finds one has found a treasure.
Sirach 6:15: faithful friends are beyond price; no amount can balance their worth.
Sirach 6:16: faithful friends are life-saving medicine, and those who fear the lord will find them.
Sirach 6:17: those who fear the lord direct their friendship aright, for as they are, so are their neighbors also.
Sirach 6:18: blessings of wisdom my child, from your youth choose discipline, and when you have gray hair you will find wisdom.
Sirach 6:19: come to her like one who plows and sows, and wait for her good harvest. for when you cultivate her you will toil but little, and soon you will eat of her produce.
Sirach 6:20: she seems very harsh to the undisciplined; fools will not remain with her.
Sirach 6:21: she will be like a heavy stone to test them, and they will not delay in casting her aside.
Sirach 6:22: for wisdom is like her name; she is not readily perceived by many.
Sirach 6:23: listen, my child, and accept my judgment; do not reject my counsel.
Sirach 6:24: put your feet into her fetters and your neck into her collar.
Sirach 6:25: bend your shoulder and carry her, and do not become angry with her bonds.
Sirach 6:26: come to her with all your soul, and keep her ways with all your might.
Sirach 6:27: search out and seek, and she will become known to you, and when you get hold of her, do not let her go.
Sirach 6:28: for at last you will find her rest, and she will be changed into joy for you.
Sirach 6:29: then her fetters will become for you a strong defense, and her collar a glorious robe.
Sirach 6:30: her yoke is a golden ornament and her bonds a purple cord.
Sirach 6:31: you will wear her like a glorious robe and put her on like a splendid crown.
Sirach 6:32: if you are willing, my child, you can be disciplined, and if you apply yourself you will become clever.
Sirach 6:33: if you love to listen you will accept discipline, and if you pay attention you will become wise.
Sirach 6:34: stand in the company of the elders. who is wise? attach yourself to such a one.
Sirach 6:35: be ready to listen to every godly discourse, and let no wise proverbs escape you.
Sirach 6:36: if you see an intelligent person, rise early to visit him; let your foot wear out his doorstep.
Sirach 6:37: reflect on the statutes of the lord, and meditate at all times on his commandments. it is he who will give insight to your mind, and your desire for wisdom will be granted.
Sirach 7:1: do no evil, and evil will never overtake you.
Sirach 7:2: stay away from wrong, and it will turn away from you.
Sirach 7:3: do not sow in the furrows of injustice, and you will not reap a sevenfold crop.
Sirach 7:4: do not seek from the lord high office or the seat of honor from the king.
Sirach 7:5: do not assert your righteousness before the lord or display your wisdom before the king.
Sirach 7:6: do not seek to become a judge, or you may be unable to root out injustice; perhaps you will fear the powerful and so mar your integrity.
Sirach 7:7: commit no offense against the public, and do not disgrace yourself among the people.
Sirach 7:8: do not commit a sin twice; even for one you will not go unpunished.
Sirach 7:9: do not say, “he will consider the great number of my gifts, and when i make an offering to the most high god, he will accept it.”
Sirach 7:10: do not grow weary when you pray; do not neglect to give alms.
Sirach 7:11: do not ridicule a person who is embittered in spirit, for there is one who humbles and exalts.
Sirach 7:12: do not devise a lie against your brother or do the same to a friend.
Sirach 7:13: refuse to utter any lie, for it is a habit that results in no good.
Sirach 7:14: do not babble in the company of the elders, and do not repeat yourself when you pray.
Sirach 7:15: do not hate hard labor or farm work, which was created by the most high.
Sirach 7:16: do not enroll in the ranks of sinners; remember that retribution will not delay.
Sirach 7:17: humble yourself to the utmost, for the punishment of the ungodly is fire and worms.
Sirach 7:18: relations with others do not exchange a friend for money or a real brother for the gold of ophir.
Sirach 7:19: do not dismiss a wise and good wife, for her charm is worth more than gold.
Sirach 7:20: do not abuse slaves who work faithfully or hired laborers who give of themselves.
Sirach 7:21: let your soul love intelligent slaves; do not withhold from them their freedom.
Sirach 7:22: do you have cattle? look after them; if they are profitable to you, keep them.
Sirach 7:23: do you have children? discipline them, and make them obedient from their youth.
Sirach 7:24: do you have daughters? be concerned for their chastity, and do not show yourself too indulgent with them.
Sirach 7:25: give a daughter in marriage, and you complete a great task, but give her to a sensible man.
Sirach 7:26: do you have a wife who pleases you? do not divorce her, but do not trust yourself to one whom you detest.
Sirach 7:27: with all your heart honor your father, and do not forget the birth pangs of your mother.
Sirach 7:28: remember that it was of your parents you were born; how will you repay what they have given to you?
Sirach 7:29: with all your soul fear the lord and revere his priests.
Sirach 7:30: with all your might love your maker, and do not neglect his ministers.
Sirach 7:31: fear the lord and honor the priest, and give him his portion, as you have been commanded: the first fruits, the purification offering, the gift of the shoulders, the sacrifice of sanctification, and the first fruits of the holy things.
Sirach 7:32: stretch out your hand to the poor, so that your blessing may be complete.
Sirach 7:33: give graciously to all the living; do not withhold kindness even from the dead.
Sirach 7:34: do not lag behind those who weep, but mourn with those who mourn.
Sirach 7:35: do not hesitate to visit the sick, because for such deeds you will be loved.
Sirach 7:36: in all you do, remember the end of your life, and then you will never sin.
Sirach 8:1: do not contend with the powerful, or you may fall into their hands.
Sirach 8:2: do not quarrel with the rich, in case their resources outweigh yours, for gold has ruined many and has perverted the minds of kings.
Sirach 8:3: do not argue with the loud of mouth, and do not heap wood on their fire.
Sirach 8:4: do not make fun of one who is uneducated, or your ancestors may be insulted.
Sirach 8:5: do not reproach one who is turning away from sin; remember that we all deserve punishment.
Sirach 8:6: do not disdain one who is old, for some of us are also growing old.
Sirach 8:7: do not rejoice over anyone’s death; remember that we must all die.
Sirach 8:8: do not slight the discourse of the sages, but turn to their maxims, because from them you will learn discipline and how to serve the great.
Sirach 8:9: do not ignore the discourse of the aged, for they themselves learned from their parents; from them you learn how to understand and to give an answer when the need arises.
Sirach 8:10: do not kindle the coals of sinners, or you may be burned in their flaming fire.
Sirach 8:11: do not let the insolent bring you to your feet, or they may lie in ambush against your words.
Sirach 8:12: do not lend to one who is stronger than you, but if you do lend anything, count it as a loss.
Sirach 8:13: do not give surety beyond your means, but if you give surety be prepared to pay.
Sirach 8:14: do not go to law against a judge, for the decision will favor him because of his standing.
Sirach 8:15: do not travel on the road with the reckless, or your troubles may become burdensome, for they will act as they please, and through their folly you will perish with them.
Sirach 8:16: do not pick a fight with the quick-tempered, and do not journey with them through a deserted region, because bloodshed means nothing to them, and where no help is at hand they will strike you down.
Sirach 8:17: do not consult with fools, for they cannot keep a secret.
Sirach 8:18: in the presence of strangers do nothing that is to be kept secret, for you do not know what they will divulge.
Sirach 8:19: do not reveal your thoughts to anyone, or you may drive away your happiness.
Sirach 9:1: do not be jealous of the wife whom you embrace, or you will teach her an evil lesson to your own hurt.
Sirach 9:2: do not give yourself to a woman and let her trample down your strength.
Sirach 9:3: do not go near a loose woman, or you may fall into her snares.
Sirach 9:4: do not dally with a female singer, or you may be caught in her activities.
Sirach 9:5: do not look intently at a virgin, or you may stumble and incur penalties for her.
Sirach 9:6: do not give yourself to prostitutes, or you may lose your inheritance.
Sirach 9:7: do not look around in the streets of a city or wander about in its deserted sections.
Sirach 9:8: turn away your eyes from a shapely woman, and do not gaze at beauty belonging to another; many have been seduced by a woman’s beauty, and by it passion is kindled like a fire.
Sirach 9:9: never dine with another man’s wife or revel with her at wine, or your heart may turn aside to her, and in blood you may plunge into destruction.
Sirach 9:10: choice of friends do not abandon old friends, for new ones cannot equal them. a new friend is like new wine; when it has aged, you will drink it with pleasure.
Sirach 9:11: do not envy the notoriety of sinners, for you do not know what their end will be like.
Sirach 9:12: do not delight in what pleases the ungodly; remember that they will not be held guiltless until hades.
Sirach 9:13: keep far from those who have power to kill, and you will not be haunted by the fear of death. but if you approach them, make no misstep, or they may rob you of your life. know that you are stepping among snares and that you are walking on the city battlements.
Sirach 9:14: as much as you can, aim to know your neighbors, and consult with the wise.
Sirach 9:15: let your conversation be with intelligent people, and let all your discussion be about the law of the most high.
Sirach 9:16: let the righteous be your dinner companions, and let your boast be in the fear of the lord.
Sirach 9:17: concerning rulers a work is praised for the skill of the artisan, so a people’s leader is proved wise by his words.
Sirach 9:18: the loud of mouth are feared in their city, and the one who is reckless in speech is hated.
Sirach 10:1: a wise magistrate educates his people, and the rule of an intelligent person is well ordered.
Sirach 10:2: as the people’s judge is, so are his officials; as the ruler of the city is, so are all its inhabitants.
Sirach 10:3: an undisciplined king ruins his people, but a city becomes fit to live in through the understanding of its rulers.
Sirach 10:4: the government of the earth is in the hand of the lord, and over it he will raise up the right leader for the time.
Sirach 10:5: human success is in the hand of the lord, and it is he who confers honor upon the lawgiver.
Sirach 10:6: the sin of pride do not get angry with your neighbor for every injury, and do not resort to acts of insolence.
Sirach 10:7: arrogance is hateful to the lord and to mortals, and injustice is outrageous to both.
Sirach 10:8: sovereignty passes from nation to nation on account of injustice and insolence and wealth.
Sirach 10:9: how can dust and ashes be proud? even in life the human body is infested with worms.
Sirach 10:10: a long illness mocks the physician; the king of today will die tomorrow.
Sirach 10:11: for when humans die they inherit maggots and vermin and worms.
Sirach 10:12: the beginning of human pride is to forsake the lord; the heart has withdrawn from its maker.
Sirach 10:13: for the beginning of pride is sin, and the one who clings to it pours out abominations. therefore the lord brought upon them unheard-of calamities and destroyed them completely.
Sirach 10:14: the lord overthrew the thrones of rulers and enthroned the lowly in their place.
Sirach 10:15: the lord plucked up the roots of the nations and planted the humble in their place.
Sirach 10:16: the lord laid waste the lands of the nations and destroyed them to the foundations of the earth.
Sirach 10:17: he removed some of them and destroyed them and erased the memory of them from the earth.
Sirach 10:18: pride was not created for human beings or violent anger for those born of women.
Sirach 10:19: persons deserving honor whose offspring are worthy of honor? human offspring. whose offspring are worthy of honor? those who fear the lord. whose offspring are unworthy of honor? human offspring. whose offspring are unworthy of honor? those who break the commandments.
Sirach 10:20: among family members their leader is worthy of honor, but those who fear the lord are worthy of honor in his eyes.
Sirach 10:22: the guest and the stranger and the poor— their boast is the fear of the lord.
Sirach 10:23: it is not right to despise one who is intelligent but poor, and it is not proper to honor one who is sinful.
Sirach 10:24: the prince and the judge and the ruler are honored, but none of them is greater than the one who fears the lord.
Sirach 10:25: free people will serve a wise slave, and an intelligent person will not complain.
Sirach 10:26: concerning humility do not make a display of your wisdom when you do your work, and do not extol yourself when you are in difficulty.
Sirach 10:27: better those who work and have plenty than those who boast and lack bread.
Sirach 10:28: my child, honor yourself with humility, and give yourself the esteem you deserve.
Sirach 10:29: who will acquit those who condemn themselves, and who will honor those who dishonor themselves?
Sirach 10:30: the poor are honored for their knowledge, while the rich are honored for their wealth.
Sirach 10:31: one who is honored in poverty, how much more in wealth! and one dishonored in wealth, how much more in poverty!
Sirach 11:1: the wisdom of the humble lifts their heads high and seats them among the great.
Sirach 11:2: do not praise individuals for their good looks or loathe anyone because of appearance alone.
Sirach 11:3: the bee is small among flying creatures, but what it produces is the origin of sweet things.
Sirach 11:4: do not mock those wearing only a loincloth or make fun of those whose day is bitter, for the works of the lord are wonderful and his works are concealed from humans.
Sirach 11:5: many oppressed have sat upon a throne, and one whom no one expected has worn a crown.
Sirach 11:6: many rulers have been utterly disgraced, and the honored have been handed over to others.
Sirach 11:7: deliberation and caution do not find fault before you investigate; examine first and then criticize.
Sirach 11:8: do not answer before you listen, and do not interrupt when another is speaking.
Sirach 11:9: do not argue about a matter that does not concern you, and do not sit with sinners when they judge a case.
Sirach 11:10: my child, do not busy yourself with many matters; if you multiply activities, you will not be held blameless. if you pursue, you will not overtake, and by fleeing you will not escape.
Sirach 11:11: there are those who work and struggle and hurry but are so much the more in want.
Sirach 11:12: there are others who are slow and need help, who lack strength and abound in poverty, but the eyes of the lord look kindly upon them; he lifts them out of their lowly condition
Sirach 11:13: and raises up their heads to the amazement of the many.
Sirach 11:14: good things and bad, life and death, poverty and wealth, come from the lord.
Sirach 11:17: the lord’s gift remains with the devout, and his favor brings lasting success.
Sirach 11:18: a person becomes rich through diligence and self-denial, and the reward allotted to him is this:
Sirach 11:19: when he says, “i have found rest, and now i shall feast on my goods!” he does not realize how time passes by; he will leave them to others and will die.
Sirach 11:20: stand by your agreement and attend to it, and grow old in your work.
Sirach 11:21: do not wonder at the works of a sinner, but trust in the lord and keep at your job, for it is easy in the sight of the lord to make the poor person suddenly rich, in an instant.
Sirach 11:22: the blessing of the lord is the reward of the pious, and quickly his blessing flourishes.
Sirach 11:23: do not say, “what do i need, and what further benefit can be mine?”
Sirach 11:24: do not say, “i have enough, and what harm can come to me now?”
Sirach 11:25: in the day of prosperity, adversity is forgotten, and in the day of adversity, prosperity is not remembered.
Sirach 11:26: for it is easy for the lord on the day of death to reward individuals according to their conduct.
Sirach 11:27: an hour’s misery makes one forget delights, and at the close of one’s life one’s deeds are revealed.
Sirach 11:28: call no one happy before his death; by how he ends, a person becomes known.
Sirach 11:29: care in choosing friends do not invite everyone into your home, for many are the tricks of the crafty.
Sirach 11:30: like a decoy partridge in a cage, so is the mind of the proud, and like spies they observe your weakness,
Sirach 11:31: for they lie in wait, turning good into evil, and to worthy actions they attach blame.
Sirach 11:32: from a spark many coals are kindled, and a sinner lies in wait to shed blood.
Sirach 11:33: beware of scoundrels, for they devise evil, and they may ruin your reputation forever.
Sirach 11:34: receive strangers into your home, and they will stir up trouble for you and will make you a stranger to your own family.
Sirach 12:1: if you do good, know to whom you do it, and you will be thanked for your good deeds.
Sirach 12:2: do good to the devout, and you will be repaid— if not by them, certainly by the most high.
Sirach 12:3: no good comes to one who persists in evil or to one who does not give alms.
Sirach 12:4: give to the devout, but do not help the sinner.
Sirach 12:5: do good to the humble, but do not give to the ungodly; hold back their bread, and do not give it to them, for by means of it they might subdue you; then you will receive twice as much evil for all the good you have done to them.

Sirach 12:7: give to the one who is good, but do not help the sinner.
Sirach 12:8: a friend is not known in prosperity, nor is an enemy hidden in adversity.
Sirach 12:9: one’s enemies are friendly when one prospers, but in adversity even one’s friend disappears.
Sirach 12:10: never trust your enemy, for like corrosion in copper, so is his wickedness.

Sirach 12:12: do not put him next to you, or he may overthrow you and take your place. do not let him sit at your right hand, or else he may try to take your own seat, and at last you will acknowledge my words and be stung by what i have said.

Sirach 12:15: they stand by you for a while, but if you falter, they will not be there.

Sirach 13:1: whoever touches pitch gets dirty, and whoever associates with the proud will become like them.

Sirach 13:5: if you own something, they will live with you; they will drain your resources without a qualm.
Sirach 13:6: when they need you, they will deceive you and will smile at you and encourage you; they will speak to you kindly and say, “what do you need?”
Sirach 13:7: they will embarrass you with their delicacies, until they have drained you two or three times, and finally they will laugh at you. should they see you afterwards, they will pass you by and shake their heads at you.

Sirach 13:10: do not be forward, or you may be rebuffed; do not stand aloof, or you will be forgotten.
Sirach 13:11: do not try to treat them as equals or trust their lengthy conversations, for they will test you by prolonged talk, and while they smile they will be examining you.
Sirach 13:12: cruel are those who do not keep your secrets; they will not spare you harm or imprisonment.
Sirach 13:13: be on your guard and very careful, for you are walking about with your own downfall.
Sirach 13:15: every creature loves its like and every person a neighbor.
Sirach 13:16: all living beings associate with their own kind, and people stick close to those like themselves.
Sirach 13:17: what does a wolf have in common with a lamb? no more has a sinner with the devout.
Sirach 13:18: what peace is there between a hyena and a dog, and what peace between the rich and the poor?

Sirach 13:24: riches are good if they are free from sin; poverty is evil only in the opinion of the ungodly.
Sirach 13:25: the heart changes the countenance either for good or for evil.
Sirach 13:26: the sign of a happy heart is a cheerful face, but to devise proverbs requires strenuous thinking.
Sirach 14:1: happy are those who do not blunder with their lips and are not stricken with grief for sin.

Sirach 14:4: what they deny themselves they collect for others, and others will live in luxury on their goods.
Sirach 14:5: if they are mean to themselves, to whom will they be generous? they will not enjoy their own riches.
Sirach 14:6: no one is worse than those who are grudging to themselves; this is the repayment for their meanness.

Sirach 14:8: misers are evil people; they turn away and disregard people.

Sirach 14:17: all living beings become old like a garment, for the decree from of old is, “you must die!”
Sirach 14:18: like abundant leaves on a spreading tree that sheds some and puts forth others, so are the generations of flesh and blood: one dies, and another is born.
Sirach 14:19: every work decays and ceases to exist, and the one who made it will pass away with it.
Sirach 14:20: the happiness of seeking wisdom happy are those who meditate on wisdom and who reason intelligently,
Sirach 14:21: who reflect in their hearts on her ways and ponder her secrets,
Sirach 14:22: pursuing her like a hunter and lying in wait on her paths;
Sirach 14:23: who peer through her windows and listen at her doors;
Sirach 14:24: who camp near her house and fasten their tent pegs to her walls;
Sirach 14:25: who pitch their tents near her and so occupy an excellent lodging place;

Sirach 15:1: whoever fears the lord will do this, and whoever holds to the law will obtain wisdom.

Sirach 16:1: do not desire a multitude of worthless children, and do not rejoice in ungodly offspring.

Sirach 16:19: together the mountains and the foundations of the earth shake and tremble when he looks upon them.

Sirach 16:24: god’s wisdom seen in creation listen to me, my child, and acquire knowledge, and pay close attention to my words.
Sirach 16:25: i will impart discipline precisely and declare knowledge accurately.
Sirach 16:26: when the lord created his works from the beginning and, in making them, determined their boundaries,
Sirach 16:27: he arranged their works in an eternal order and their dominion for all generations. they neither hunger nor grow weary, and they do not abandon their tasks.
Sirach 16:28: they do not crowd one another, and they never disobey his word.

Sirach 17:6: discretion and tongue and eyes, ears and a mind for thinking he gave them.

Sirach 17:28: from the dead, as from one who does not exist, thanksgiving has ceased; those who are alive and well sing the lord’s praises.

Sirach 18:1: he who lives forever created the whole universe;
Sirach 18:2: the lord alone will be justified.

Sirach 18:5: who can measure his majestic power, and who can fully recount his mercies?
Sirach 18:6: it is not possible to diminish or increase them, nor is it possible to fathom the wonders of the lord.

Sirach 18:13: the compassion of humans is for their neighbors, but the compassion of the lord is for every living thing. he rebukes and trains and teaches them and turns them back, as a shepherd his flock.
Sirach 18:14: he has compassion on those who accept his discipline and who are eager for his decrees.
Sirach 18:15: the right spirit in giving alms my child, do not mix reproach with your good deeds or harsh words with any gift.
Sirach 18:16: does not the dew give relief from the scorching heat? so a word is better than a gift.
Sirach 18:17: indeed, does not a word surpass a good gift? both are to be found in a gracious person.
Sirach 18:18: a fool will rebuke ungraciously, and the gift of a grudging giver makes the eyes weary.
Sirach 18:19: the need of reflection and self-control before you speak, learn, and before you fall ill, take care of yourself.

Sirach 18:21: before falling ill, humble yourself, and when you have sinned, repent.

Sirach 18:26: from morning to evening conditions change; all things move swiftly before the lord.
Sirach 18:27: one who is wise is cautious in everything; when sin is all around, one guards against wrongdoing.
Sirach 18:28: every intelligent person knows wisdom and praises the one who finds her.
Sirach 18:29: those who are skilled in words become wise themselves and pour forth apt proverbs.
Sirach 18:30: self-control do not follow your base desires but restrain your appetites.
Sirach 18:31: if you allow your soul to take pleasure in base desire, it will make you the laughingstock of your enemies.
Sirach 18:32: do not revel in great luxury, or you may become impoverished by contact with it.

Sirach 19:1: the one who does this will not become rich; one who despises small things will fail little by little.

Sirach 19:5: one who rejoices in wickedness will be condemned,
Sirach 19:6: but one who hates discussion lacks understanding.

Sirach 19:10: have you heard something? let it die with you. be brave; it will not make you burst!
Sirach 19:11: having heard something, the fool suffers birth pangs like a woman in labor with a child.
Sirach 19:12: like an arrow stuck in a person’s thigh, so is gossip in the belly of a fool.
Sirach 19:13: question a friend; perhaps he did not do it; or if he did, so that he may not do it again.

Sirach 19:28: even if lack of strength keeps them from sinning, they will nevertheless do evil when they find the opportunity.

Sirach 20:1: there is a rebuke that is untimely, and there is the person who is wise enough to keep silent.
